description: Repository skeleton for the custom integration exists
steps: Create custom_components/intergas_xtend/__init__.py with empty async_setup_entry and async_unload_entry
Create manifest.json with domain intergas_xtend, name 'Intergas Xtend', version 0.1.0, iot_class local_polling, config_flow true, empty requirements, codeowners, documentation and issue_tracker URLs
Create const.py with DOMAIN, DEFAULT_HOST = '10.20.30.1', DEFAULT_SCAN_INTERVAL = 10, MIN_SCAN_INTERVAL = 5, MAX_SCAN_INTERVAL = 60
Create hacs.json with name and minimum HA version
Create .gitignore for Python, .venv, .pytest_cache, .ruff_cache
Create requirements_dev.txt with homeassistant, pytest-homeassistant-custom-component, ruff
Create pyproject.toml with ruff and pytest config (asyncio_mode auto, testpaths tests)
Verify: python -c 'import json; json.load(open("custom_components/intergas_xtend/manifest.json"))' succeeds

description: GitHub Actions validate the integration on push
steps: Create .github/workflows/validate.yml
Add job running home-assistant/actions/hassfest
Add job running hacs/action with category integration
Add job running ruff check and pytest
Verify: workflow file parses and all three jobs are listed

description: Field list and endpoint path live in one place
steps: In const.py add STATS_PATH = '/api/stats/values'
Add a comment stating the source: docs/stats-mapping.md and a capture from the device on 2026-10-06
Verify: len(STATS_FIELDS) == 32 and no duplicates

description: api.py fetches the status payload without importing Home Assistant
steps: Create api.py with exceptions XtendError, XtendConnectionError(XtendError), XtendResponseError(XtendError)
Add class XtendApi(session: aiohttp.ClientSession, host: str) with method async_get_stats() -> dict[str, int | str]
Build the URL as http://{host}/api/stats/values?fields={','.join(STATS_FIELDS)}
Use a 5 second total timeout; on aiohttp.ClientError or asyncio.TimeoutError raise XtendConnectionError
On HTTP status other than 200 raise XtendResponseError with the status code
Verify: grep for 'homeassistant' in api.py returns nothing

description: Parser accepts the real response shape and rejects anything else
steps: Parse the body as JSON; on JSONDecodeError raise XtendResponseError
Require a top-level 'stats' key that is a dict; otherwise raise XtendResponseError
Return the inner dict unchanged: integer values stay int, string values (47e0) stay str
Do not apply scaling or sentinel handling in api.py; that belongs to the sensor layer
Verify: parsing the fixture returns a dict with 32 keys and stats['47e0'] == 'V1.20-'

description: Test fixture holds the captured device response verbatim
steps: Create tests/__init__.py and tests/conftest.py enabling custom integrations (auto_enable_custom_integrations fixture)
Add conftest fixtures 'stats_payload', 'stats_payload_standby' and 'stats_payload_n095' that load these files
Verify: pytest --collect-only runs without import errors

description: api.py is covered by unit tests against a mocked HTTP server
steps: Create tests/test_api.py using aioresponses or aiohttp test_utils
Test: 200 with fixture body returns the 32-key dict
Test: connection refused raises XtendConnectionError
Test: timeout raises XtendConnectionError
Test: HTTP 500 raises XtendResponseError
Test: body 'not json' raises XtendResponseError
Test: body {"other": {}} raises XtendResponseError
Test: the requested URL contains fields= with all 32 ids in order
Verify: pytest tests/test_api.py passes

description: User can add the integration with host and poll interval
steps: Create config_flow.py with ConfigFlow for DOMAIN, VERSION = 1
Step 'user' shows a form with host (default 10.20.30.1) and scan_interval (default 10, min 5, max 60)
On submit call XtendApi.async_get_stats once using async_get_clientsession(hass)
Map XtendConnectionError to error 'cannot_connect' and XtendResponseError to 'invalid_response'
Set unique_id to the host and abort with 'already_configured' if it exists
Create the entry with title 'Intergas Xtend ({host})' and data {host, scan_interval}
Verify: strings.json has config.step.user, config.error.cannot_connect, config.error.invalid_response, config.abort.already_configured

description: Poll interval can be changed afterwards via options
steps: Add OptionsFlow with one field scan_interval (min 5, max 60), prefilled from options or data
In __init__.py register an update listener that reloads the entry when options change
Coordinator reads scan_interval from entry.options first, then entry.data
Verify: changing the option and saving triggers a reload and the new interval is in use

description: Translations exist in English and Dutch
steps: Create strings.json with all config and options texts in English
Create translations/en.json as a copy of strings.json
Create translations/nl.json with Dutch texts
Verify: both translation files are valid JSON and have the same key structure as strings.json

description: Config flow is covered by tests
steps: Create tests/test_config_flow.py with XtendApi.async_get_stats patched
Test: happy path with defaults creates an entry with host 10.20.30.1 and scan_interval 10
Test: XtendConnectionError shows form with error cannot_connect
Test: XtendResponseError shows form with error invalid_response
Test: second flow for the same host aborts with already_configured
Test: options flow updates scan_interval
Verify: pytest tests/test_config_flow.py passes

description: One coordinator polls the device at the configured interval
steps: Create coordinator.py with XtendCoordinator(DataUpdateCoordinator[dict[str, int | str]])
update_interval = timedelta(seconds=scan_interval from options or data)
_async_update_data calls XtendApi.async_get_stats; wrap XtendError in UpdateFailed
In __init__.py create the coordinator, call async_config_entry_first_refresh, store it in entry.runtime_data
Forward setup to platform sensor only
Verify: after setup the coordinator has data with 32 keys and last_update_success is True

description: When the Xtend is unreachable the coordinator backs off instead of hammering
steps: Count consecutive failures in the coordinator; reset to 0 on success
Add BACKOFF_START_FAILURES = 3, BACKOFF_FACTOR = 2, BACKOFF_MAX_SECONDS = 300 to const.py
From the 3rd consecutive failure on, set update_interval to min(scan_interval * 2 ** (failures - 2), 300) seconds
On the first success restore update_interval to the configured scan_interval
Log one warning when backoff starts and one info line when it ends; do not log every failed poll above debug
Verify: with scan_interval 10 the intervals after failures 1..7 are 10, 10, 20, 40, 80, 160, 300

description: Losing the access point is visible to the user with instructions
steps: After 3 consecutive failures create a repairs issue 'ap_unreachable' (severity warning, not fixable)

Issue text: the Xtend at {host} is unreachable; the AP switches off after about 15 minutes without requests; re-enable the AP on the Xtend, reconnect the HA host Wi-Fi if needed, then press the 'Poll now' button
On the next success delete the repairs issue
Add the repairs issue texts to strings.json and both translation files (NL: 'Nu pollen' for the button name)
Verify: with 3 failed updates the issue exists; after one success it is gone

description: User can force a poll with a button; a successful poll resumes normal polling
steps: Add platform button to the forwarded platforms in __init__.py
Create button.py with one XtendPollNowButton(CoordinatorEntity, ButtonEntity): translation_key poll_now, EN name 'Poll now', NL name 'Nu pollen', entity_category DIAGNOSTIC, icon mdi:refresh
The button must stay available when the coordinator has failed (override available to return True), otherwise it cannot be pressed when needed
async_press calls coordinator.async_request_refresh()
In the coordinator, a successful refresh (manual or scheduled) resets the failure counter and restores the configured scan_interval, so one successful manual poll ends the backoff
A failed manual poll keeps the current backoff interval and does not increase it
Verify: after 5 failures and interval 80 s, a successful press makes update_interval 10 s again and the repairs issue disappears

description: All entities belong to one device with firmware and link
steps: Build DeviceInfo with identifiers {(DOMAIN, host)}, name 'Intergas Xtend', manufacturer 'Intergas'
Set sw_version from stats['47e0'] when it is a string
Set configuration_url to http://{host}
Verify: the device registry shows one device with sw_version V1.20- for the fixture

description: Sensor definitions are one table in const.py driven by docs/stats-mapping.md
steps: In descriptions.py (not const.py: api.py imports const.py and must stay free of Home Assistant imports, decided 2026-10-07) define a frozen dataclass XtendSensorDescription extending SensorEntityDescription with fields: factor (float | None), none_values (frozenset[int]), text_format (str | None)
Define SENSORS: tuple[XtendSensorDescription, ...] with one entry per field in STATS_FIELDS, key = hex id
Default none_values = frozenset({32767}) for every numeric field
Add a comment above SENSORS: 'Source: docs/stats-mapping.md. Do not change factors or units without updating that file.'
Verify: {d.key for d in SENSORS} == set(STATS_FIELDS)

description: One generic sensor class converts raw values
steps: Create sensor.py with async_setup_entry creating one XtendSensor per SENSORS entry
XtendSensor(CoordinatorEntity[XtendCoordinator], SensorEntity) with has_entity_name True, unique_id f'{host}_{key}', translation_key = key-based name from the description
native_value: raw = coordinator.data.get(key); if raw is None or raw in none_values return None
If text_format is set return text_format % raw; elif factor is set return round(raw * factor, 2); else return raw
available = coordinator.last_update_success
Verify: no per-field subclasses exist in sensor.py

description: Temperature sensors
steps: Add SENSORS entries (key, translation_key, EN name, NL name): 79b3 room_temperature 'Room temperature' 'Kamertemperatuur'; 7921 room_target_temperature 'Room target temperature' 'Kamer doeltemperatuur'; 62d1 outside_temperature 'Outside temperature' 'Buitentemperatuur'; 6280 ch_return_temperature 'CH water return' 'Cv-water retour'; 621d ch_supply_temperature 'CH water supply' 'Cv-water aanvoer'; 62ed ch_setpoint 'CH water setpoint' 'Cv-water streefwaarde'; 620f aux1_temperature 'Aux 1 temperature' 'Aux 1 temperatuur'; 6206 aux2_temperature 'Aux 2 temperature' 'Aux 2 temperatuur'; 610b dhw_temperature 'DHW actual' 'Tapwater werkelijk'; 61eb dhw_setpoint 'DHW setpoint' 'Tapwater streefwaarde'
Each: factor 0.01, native_unit UnitOfTemperature.CELSIUS, device_class TEMPERATURE, state_class MEASUREMENT
Verify with stats_values_standby against the summary screenshot: 79b3 -> 22.62, 62d1 -> 16.17, 6280 -> 21.75, 621d -> 32.55, 62ed -> 20.0, 610b -> 23.15, 61eb -> 50.0

description: Power and COP sensors
steps: Add entries: 503e heat_pump_power 'Heat pump power' 'Vermogen warmtepomp'; 5088 boiler_power 'Boiler power' 'Vermogen cv-ketel'; 5077 total_thermal_power 'Total thermal power' 'Totaal thermisch vermogen'; 50f2 retrieved_power 'Retrieved power' 'Opgenomen vermogen'
Each power entry: factor 1, unit UnitOfPower.WATT, device_class POWER, state_class MEASUREMENT (the summary page shows W; raw value is already W, mapping factor 0.001 kW is the same quantity)
Add entry for 5041 cop 'COP' 'COP': factor 0.1, no unit, no device_class, state_class MEASUREMENT, icon mdi:heat-pump
Verify with stats_values: 5088 -> 7917, 50f2 -> 7, 5041 -> 0.0
Verify with stats_values_standby against the screenshot: 503e -> 0, 5088 -> 0, 5077 -> 0, 50f2 -> 7, 5041 -> 0.0

description: Flow and pressure sensors
steps: Add entry for 629c ch_flow 'CH water flow' 'Cv-water debiet': factor 0.01, unit UnitOfVolumeFlowRate.LITERS_PER_MINUTE, device_class VOLUME_FLOW_RATE, state_class MEASUREMENT
Add entry for 7ed3 ch_pressure 'CH water pressure' 'Cv-water druk': factor 0.01, unit UnitOfPressure.BAR, device_class PRESSURE, state_class MEASUREMENT
Verify with stats_values: 629c -> 14.91, 7ed3 -> 2.01
Verify with stats_values_standby against the screenshot: 629c -> 15.03, 7ed3 -> 1.85

description: Domestic hot water (Xtore) sensors
steps: Add entry for 6115 dhw_available 'DHW available' 'Tapwater beschikbaar': factor 0.01, unit PERCENTAGE, state_class MEASUREMENT
Add entry for 61ba dhw_volume 'DHW volume' 'Tapwater inhoud': factor 1, unit UnitOfVolume.LITERS, device_class VOLUME_STORAGE, entity_category DIAGNOSTIC
Verify with stats_values: 6115 -> None (32767), 61ba -> 80
Verify with stats_values_standby against the screenshot: 6115 -> 100.0, 61ba -> 80

description: Notification, lockout and fault code sensors
steps: Add entry for 7940 notification_code 'Notification code' 'Notificatiecode': none_values {255}, text_format 'n%03d', entity_category DIAGNOSTIC
Add entry for 7e2c lockout_code 'Lockout code' 'Lockout-code': none_values {255}, text_format 'F%03d', entity_category DIAGNOSTIC
Add entry for 8439 boiler_fault_code 'Boiler fault code' 'Foutcode cv-ketel': none_values {0}, no factor, entity_category DIAGNOSTIC
Verify with stats_values: all three return None; with 7e2c = 37 the value is 'F037'
Verify with stats_values_n095 (real capture while the display showed n095, confirmed by the owner on 2026-10-06): 7940 -> 'n095', 7e2c -> None, 8439 -> None

description: Code sensors carry the manual's description and cause/solution as attributes
steps: Create codes.py in the integration with FAULT_CODES: dict[str, CodeInfo] and NOTIFICATION_CODES: dict[str, CodeInfo], where CodeInfo is a frozen dataclass (description: str, cause_solution: tuple[str, ...])

Fill both dicts from docs/fault-codes.json; keys are the code strings 'F001'..'F254' and 'n000'..'n097'. Keep the Dutch text exactly as in the file (it is quoted from the manual; attribute values cannot be translated by HA)
Handle the range entry n100-n165: a lookup helper notification_info(code) returns the FOTA entry for n100 up to and including n165
Add a comment above the dicts: 'Source: docs/fault-codes.json, generated from Intergas document 88104401 chapter 12.1 and 12.2. Regenerate, do not edit by hand.'

In XtendSensor add extra_state_attributes for keys 7940 and 7e2c: {'description': ..., 'cause_solution': [...]} looked up by the formatted value; when the value is None or the code is unknown return {'description': None, 'cause_solution': []}
Field 8439 gets no attributes: it holds the CV boiler's own OpenTherm fault code, which is not in this manual

scripts/gen_codes.py (added 2026-10-06) regenerates docs/fault-codes.json and docs/fault-codes.md from the PDF with pdfplumber (page index 84-87); run it again when a new manual version appears: python -I -X utf8 scripts/gen_codes.py <pdf> docs/fault-codes.md docs/fault-codes.json

Verify with stats_values_n095: the sensor state is 'n095', attribute description is 'Probleem met driewegklep.' and cause_solution has 4 items; with 7940 = 120 description is 'FOTA gerelateerde melding.'; with 7e2c = 254 description is 'Bypassmodus actief.'

description: Firmware version sensor
steps: Add entry for 47e0 firmware_version 'Firmware version' 'Firmwareversie': no factor, none_values empty, entity_category DIAGNOSTIC, icon mdi:chip
native_value returns the string unchanged
Verify with fixture: value is 'V1.20-'

description: Raw bitfield and unknown fields are exposed as disabled diagnostics
steps: Add entries: 7e51 heat_demand_status 'Heat demand status (raw)' 'Warmtevraagstatus (ruw)'; 7e7a burner_status 'Burner status (raw)' 'Branderstatus (ruw)'; 77c3 status_flags 'Status flags (raw)' 'Statusvlaggen (ruw)'; 77d2 system_io 'System I/O (raw)' 'Systeem-I/O (ruw)'; f9f2 bivalent_service_flags 'Bivalent service flags (raw)' 'Vlaggen hybride regeling (ruw)'; 6101 raw_6101 'Raw 6101' 'Ruw 6101'; 6117 raw_6117 'Raw 6117' 'Ruw 6117'; 7774 raw_7774 'Raw 7774' 'Ruw 7774'; 77de raw_77de 'Raw 77de' 'Ruw 77de'
Each: no factor, none_values empty, entity_category DIAGNOSTIC, entity_registry_enabled_default False
Verify with stats_values: 77d2 -> 17102, 7774 -> 255 (not None)

description: Entity names are translated
steps: Add entity.sensor.<translation_key>.name for every SENSORS entry to strings.json and translations/en.json using the EN names listed in the entity items above
Add the NL names listed in the entity items above to translations/nl.json
Source of the names: the Xtend summary page ('Xtend summary' / 'Xtend overzicht'); fields not on that page use docs/stats-mapping.md
Verify: every translation_key in SENSORS has a name in all three files and the key sets are identical

description: Derived states from the summary page are mapped to raw fields (not required for phase 1)
steps: The summary page shows states that are not a single stats field: Operating mode (Standby), Silent mode (Off), Heat demand heat pump (Off), Heat demand boiler (Off), DHW State (Standby)
Candidate sources: 7e51 heat demand status, 7e7a burner status, 77c3 status flags, 6117 (DHW group), f9f2 bivalent service flags
Collect at least 10 captures of the full stats payload together with the summary page states, covering: standby, CH heating by heat pump, CH heating by boiler, DHW run, silent mode on

Start the table with the three fixtures already in tests/fixtures: stats_values (7e51 206, 77c3 208, f9f2 265, 6117 3), stats_values_standby (page: Standby, heat demand off, DHW Standby; 7e51 126, 77c3 0, f9f2 8, 6117 0), stats_values_n095 (heat pump 5000 W, DHW setpoint 65 °C; 7e51 206, 77c3 194, f9f2 136, 6117 3)
Record each capture as a row in docs/derived-states.md: timestamp, page states, values of 7e51, 7e7a, 77c3, 6117, f9f2
Only when a bit or value maps one-to-one in every capture: add the mapping to docs/stats-mapping.md and create a prd item for a binary_sensor or enum sensor
Verify: docs/derived-states.md exists with at least 10 rows, or this item stays passes false

description: Coordinator behaviour is covered by tests
steps: Create tests/test_coordinator.py with a helper that sets up a config entry with XtendApi patched
Test: successful setup gives coordinator.data equal to the fixture
Test: an update raising XtendConnectionError marks a sensor as unavailable
Test: a following successful update makes the sensor available again
Test: 3 consecutive failures create the repairs issue, 1 success removes it
Test: backoff sequence with scan_interval 10 is 10, 10, 20, 40, 80, 160, 300 and stays at 300
Test: pressing button.intergas_xtend_poll_now during backoff triggers a refresh; on success update_interval is back to 10 and the failure counter is 0
Test: the poll now button is available while sensors are unavailable
Test: update_interval equals scan_interval from options when options are set
Verify: pytest tests/test_coordinator.py passes

description: Sensor conversion is covered by tests
steps: Create tests/test_sensor.py
Test: sensor.intergas_xtend_room_temperature state is '26.41' with unit °C
Test: with stats_payload_standby the states match the summary screenshot: room 22.62, outside 16.17, CH pressure 1.85, CH flow 15.03, retrieved power 7, DHW available 100.0
Test: sensor for 6206 has state 'unknown'

Test: with stats_payload sensor for 7940 has state 'unknown' and attributes description None, cause_solution []; with stats_payload_n095 state is 'n095', description 'Probleem met driewegklep.', cause_solution 4 items
Test: with payload 7940 = 120 the description is 'FOTA gerelateerde melding.' (range n100-n165); with 7940 = 99 (not in manual) state is 'n099' and description None
Test: with payload 7e2c = 254 state is 'F254' and description 'Bypassmodus actief.'
Test: codes.py covers every code in docs/fault-codes.json (19 fault codes, 57 single notification codes plus the n100-n165 range)
Test: sensor for 77d2 is diagnostic and disabled by default in the entity registry
Test: exactly 32 sensor entities and 1 button entity are registered
Verify: pytest tests/test_sensor.py passes

description: Lint, format and test suite are clean
steps: Run ruff check . and fix every finding
Run ruff format . and commit the result
Run pytest and confirm every test passes
Verify: all three commands exit with code 0

description: Field mapping is stored in the repository
steps: Create docs/stats-mapping.md with the mapping document exactly as provided by the owner
Reference docs/stats-mapping.md from AGENTS.md and from the comment above SENSORS in descriptions.py
Verify: every id in STATS_FIELDS appears in docs/stats-mapping.md

description: Fault and notification codes from the manual are stored in the repository
steps: docs/fault-codes.md and docs/fault-codes.json hold chapter 12.1 and 12.2 of Intergas document 88104401 (Xtend Eco installatievoorschrift), extracted 2026-10-06 with pdfplumber
Text is kept exactly as printed, including the manual's own spelling
Verify: fault-codes.json has 19 fault_codes and 58 notification_codes entries, the last one being the n100-n165 range

description: README explains installation and the access point behaviour
steps: Add section Installation: add repository in HACS as integration, restart, add integration 'Intergas Xtend'
Add section Network: HA host must be joined to the Xtend Wi-Fi AP; default IP 10.20.30.1

Add section Access point timeout: the AP switches off after about 15 minutes without requests; polling keeps it alive; when unreachable the integration backs off to at most 5 minutes; how to recover: re-enable the AP, reconnect Wi-Fi on the HA host if needed, press 'Poll now'

Add section Entities: table of the 32 sensors with unit and whether they are enabled by default; explain that the notification and lockout code sensors carry description and cause_solution attributes in Dutch, taken from the manual (link docs/fault-codes.md)
Add note: the unique id is the host; changing the IP creates a new entry
Add note: minimum Home Assistant 2025.11.0, the first release that runs on Python 3.14 (hacs.json, decided 2026-10-07)
Verify: README has these five sections

description: Integration works against the real device
steps: Copy custom_components/intergas_xtend into the config directory of a Home Assistant instance and restart
Add the integration with the default host 10.20.30.1
Verify: the device appears with sw_version and 32 sensors
Verify: room temperature, outdoor temperature and water pressure show plausible values that change over time
Switch the AP off or wait more than 15 minutes without polling; verify sensors become unavailable, the repairs issue appears and the log shows backoff starting
Switch the AP on again and reconnect the HA host Wi-Fi if needed; press 'Poll now'; verify values return without a restart, the issue disappears and polling is back at the configured interval
